question: Does the shipped guided-capture target acquisition (region occupancy → 9-frame streak → lock; ambiguity → wrist-raise gesture; post-lock anchor following) actually work on real multi-person footage?
method: Faithful TS port of GuidedCaptureViewController.considerTargetAcquisition + ApplePoseProvider.primaryPerson (ta-replay-1, port semantics unit-tested), replayed offline against corpus recordings at ≤30fps. Cases = scene windows with a machine-proposed starting region + true target track; 7 human-verified (devin-visual-v1), 281 unverified Tier-C included only as a separate aggregate. Constants: region radius 0.17, 9-frame streak, gesture elevation 0.03, on-target radius 0.06.
findings: STICKY AMBIGUITY IS A DEAD END: once ≥2 people touch the region the state machine waits forever for a deliberate gesture; in natural footage nobody performs it → never_locked. 3/7 verified cases died here.

NATURAL FALSE GESTURES ARE REAL: 37/288 Tier-C replays 'locked' via gesture from ordinary play motion (serves, ready position raise wrists above shoulders). The gesture arbitration can pick whoever swings first, not the intended user.

POST-LOCK FOLLOWING IS THE WEAKEST STAGE: mean on-target fraction 0.584 (verified) / 0.493 (Tier-C); the span/(1+3·distance) score jumps to decisively larger newcomers (also demonstrated by unit test). Only 1/4 verified locks stayed ≥90% on-target.
LOCK LATENCY IS NOT THE PROBLEM: median 320ms once a single occupant is stable.
caveats: n=7 verified cases; wide intervals. Tier-C aggregate includes unverified machine-proposed regions/targets.
Offline people.json comes from batch extraction, not the live capture path; live jitter/dropped frames not modeled.
Machine-proposed regions equal the target's own start position by construction; real users may tap less precisely.
nextActions: Ambiguity needs a timeout → largest/closest-occupant fallback or explicit re-tap prompt (product decision, then re-measure here)
Gesture arbitration should require sustained elevation (not a single frame) and prefer the occupant nearest the region
Post-lock follower should get incumbent hysteresis like playerTracker (candidate must beat incumbent by margin); prototype offline and re-run this bench before touching Swift
